historical_record.description: A one-storey reinforced-concrete commercial building was built for the Standard Oil Company as a garage and repair shop; its footprint went unchanged through most of the twentieth century.

The Standard Oil Company — later Chevron — ran a bulk fuel terminal across this block from about 1914 to about 1974. The concrete pads of two of its fuel tanks, carried on timber piles, remain buried five to six feet below ground.
The bulk fuel facility was dismantled and the property divided into five parcels and sold; the 1910 garage had stayed in use as an auxiliary building until the sale.
Between 1974 and 2004 the building's occupants included the Pacific Telephone Company.
The building was converted from industrial use to the Axis Cafe restaurant; the work took out the vehicular bays, the original windows and the original pedestrian entrance.
The Historic Preservation Commission unanimously adopted a 6Z survey rating for the building, finding it ineligible for the National Register, the California Register and the local register.
